description: We are a team of passionate students exploring the untold stories of NASA’s hardware left on the Moon and Mars. Our project uses NASA open data to create an interactive, educational experience for school-age audiences — bringing forgotten rovers, landers, and probes back to life through storytelling. We’re looking for members with skills in web development, design, and content writing.
summary:
Remnant is an interactive educational website that brings NASA’s abandoned hardware back to life through first-person storytelling. Each of the 11 missions — across the Moon, Mars, and deep space — narrates its own story: from Surveyor 3 on the Moon (1967) to Ingenuity’s final flight on Mars (2024).

The site features a Deep Space Explorer game, a 10-question quiz with an Explorer badge, mission search and filters, a favorites system, and a live Voyager distance counter powered by NASA Eyes on the Solar System. All mission photography is sourced from NASA’s Image Library, and every fact traces back to official NASA data.

Built for school-age children worldwide, Remnant turns forgotten machines into characters kids remember — not a textbook, but an adventure.
details:
Remnant is a single-page interactive website built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, deployed on Vercel. It tells the stories of 11 NASA missions in first person — the machines themselves narrate their journeys across the Moon, Mars, and deep space.

Features include: a Deep Space Explorer game where users hunt for Voyager and Pioneer spacecraft among the stars; a 10-question quiz with an Explorer badge; mission search and filters by world and status; a favorites system using browser localStorage; a live Voyager distance counter pulling from NASA Eyes on the Solar System data; an animated rocket loading screen; and mission-specific hover animations.

All photography is sourced from NASA’s Image Library (images.nasa.gov). Mission facts trace back to NASA’s Open Data Portal (data.nasa.gov). The project was designed for school-age children to make NASA’s legacy hardware feel like characters, not history entries. Claude (Anthropic’s AI) was used to assist with writing the first-person mission narratives and debugging JavaScript code.
